From e9bbfb4bfa86c6b5515b868d6982ac60505d7e39 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Viktor Malik <vmalik@redhat.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Mar 2026 15:40:45 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] powerpc, perf: Check that current->mm is alive before getting
 user callchain

It may happen that mm is already released, which leads to kernel panic.
This adds the NULL check for current->mm, similarly to
commit 20afc60f892d ("x86, perf: Check that current->mm is alive before getting user callchain").

I was getting this panic when running a profiling BPF program
(profile.py from bcc-tools):

    [26215.051935] Kernel attempted to read user page (588) - exploit attempt? (uid: 0)
    [26215.051950] BUG: Kernel NULL pointer dereference on read at 0x00000588
    [26215.051952] Faulting instruction address: 0xc00000000020fac0
    [26215.051957] Oops: Kernel access of bad area, sig: 11 [#1]
    [...]
    [26215.052049] Call Trace:
    [26215.052050] [c000000061da6d30] [c00000000020fc10] perf_callchain_user_64+0x2d0/0x490 (unreliable)
    [26215.052054] [c000000061da6dc0] [c00000000020f92c] perf_callchain_user+0x1c/0x30
    [26215.052057] [c000000061da6de0] [c0000000005ab2a0] get_perf_callchain+0x100/0x360
    [26215.052063] [c000000061da6e70] [c000000000573bc8] bpf_get_stackid+0x88/0xf0
    [26215.052067] [c000000061da6ea0] [c008000000042258] bpf_prog_16d4ab9ab662f669_do_perf_event+0xf8/0x274
    [...]

In addition, move storing the top-level stack entry to generic
perf_callchain_user to make sure the top-evel entry is always captured,
even if current->mm is NULL.

Fixes: 20002ded4d93 ("perf_counter: powerpc: Add callchain support")
Signed-off-by: Viktor Malik <vmalik@redhat.com>
Tested-by: Qiao Zhao <qzhao@redhat.com>
Tested-by: Venkat Rao Bagalkote <venkat88@linux.ibm.com>
Reviewed-by: Saket Kumar Bhaskar <skb99@linux.ibm.com>

diff --git a/arch/powerpc/perf/callchain_32.c b/arch/powerpc/perf/callchain_32.c
index ddcc2d8aa64a..0de21c5d272c 100644
--- a/arch/powerpc/perf/callchain_32.c
+++ b/arch/powerpc/perf/callchain_32.c
@@ -142,7 +142,6 @@ void perf_callchain_user_32(struct perf_callchain_entry_ctx *entry,
 	next_ip = perf_arch_instruction_pointer(regs);
 	lr = regs->link;
 	sp = regs->gpr[1];
-	perf_callchain_store(entry, next_ip);
 
 	while (entry->nr < entry->max_stack) {
 		fp = (unsigned int __user *) (unsigned long) sp;

diff --git a/arch/powerpc/perf/callchain_64.c b/arch/powerpc/perf/callchain_64.c
index 115d1c105e8a..30fb61c5f0cb 100644
--- a/arch/powerpc/perf/callchain_64.c
+++ b/arch/powerpc/perf/callchain_64.c
@@ -77,7 +77,6 @@ void perf_callchain_user_64(struct perf_callchain_entry_ctx *entry,
 	next_ip = perf_arch_instruction_pointer(regs);
 	lr = regs->link;
 	sp = regs->gpr[1];
-	perf_callchain_store(entry, next_ip);
 
 	while (entry->nr < entry->max_stack) {
 		fp = (unsigned long __user *) sp;
-- 
2.34.1



diff --git a/arch/powerpc/perf/callchain.c b/arch/powerpc/perf/callchain.c
index 26aa26482c9a..992cc5c98214 100644
--- a/arch/powerpc/perf/callchain.c
+++ b/arch/powerpc/perf/callchain.c
@@ -103,6 +103,11 @@ perf_callchain_kernel(struct perf_callchain_entry_ctx *entry, struct pt_regs *re
 void
 perf_callchain_user(struct perf_callchain_entry_ctx *entry, struct pt_regs *regs)
 {
+	perf_callchain_store(entry, perf_arch_instruction_pointer(regs));
+
+	if (!current->mm)
+		return;
+
 	if (!is_32bit_task())
 		perf_callchain_user_64(entry, regs);
 	else

## Summary of modifications

### Modifications in each file

- **`arch/powerpc/perf/callchain.c`**:
  - Added `perf_callchain_store(entry, perf_arch_instruction_pointer(regs))` at the beginning of `perf_callchain_user()` to always record the top-level stack entry (the current instruction pointer) before any further processing.
  - Added a NULL check for `current->mm`. If `current->mm` is NULL, the function returns early, preventing the per-architecture callchain walk (which would dereference `current->mm` and cause a kernel panic).

- **`arch/powerpc/perf/callchain_32.c`**:
  - Removed the line `perf_callchain_store(entry, next_ip);` from `perf_callchain_user_32()`. This call was moved to the common `perf_callchain_user()` function.

- **`arch/powerpc/perf/callchain_64.c`**:
  - Removed the line `perf_callchain_store(entry, next_ip);` from `perf_callchain_user_64()`. This call was moved to the common `perf_callchain_user()` function.

### Relationships between changes

The central fix is in `perf_callchain_user()` (callchain.c): by capturing the top-level stack entry before checking `current->mm`, the patch ensures that this entry is always recorded, even when the process’s memory map is already released (i.e., `current->mm` is NULL). The early return when `current->mm` is NULL avoids the subsequent NULL pointer dereference that occurred when the per-architecture functions tried to access user memory.

The removal of `perf_callchain_store` from both `perf_callchain_user_32()` and `perf_callchain_user_64()` simply relocates that single store to the common entry point, eliminating duplication and making the control flow cleaner. This also ensures that the top-level entry is captured once, regardless of which architecture-specific handler is called (or even if no handler is called due to early return).

The patch fixes a kernel panic in PowerPC perf callchain handling when `current->mm` has already been released. It consists of three file modifications:

- **`arch/powerpc/perf/callchain.c`** (common user callchain entry):
  - Adds a `perf_callchain_store` for the top-level instruction pointer before any per-architecture call.
  - Adds a NULL check for `current->mm`; if NULL, returns immediately after storing the top-level entry, avoiding further user-space access that could cause a panic.

- **`arch/powerpc/perf/callchain_64.c`** (64-bit user callchain):
  - Removes the `perf_callchain_store(entry, next_ip)` call that previously stored the top-level instruction pointer, since it is now done in the common `perf_callchain_user`.

- **`arch/powerpc/perf/callchain_32.c`** (32-bit user callchain):
  - Same removal of the top-level `perf_callchain_store` call.

**Relationship:** The core fix is the addition of the `current->mm` check in `perf_callchain_user` to prevent kernel NULL pointer dereference. To ensure the top-level stack entry is always captured (even when `current->mm` is NULL), the storage of that entry is moved upward from the per-architecture functions into the common `perf_callchain_user`. This centralized placement guarantees the entry is recorded before the early return due to a NULL mm.

## Summary of Modifications

### File: `arch/powerpc/perf/callchain_32.c`
- **Removed** the line `perf_callchain_store(entry, next_ip);` from `perf_callchain_user_32()`. This line previously stored the top-level stack entry (instruction pointer from `regs`) at the start of the function.

### File: `arch/powerpc/perf/callchain_64.c`
- **Removed** the same line `perf_callchain_store(entry, next_ip);` from `perf_callchain_user_64()`.

### File: `arch/powerpc/perf/callchain.c`
- **Added** a new `perf_callchain_store(entry, perf_arch_instruction_pointer(regs));` at the beginning of `perf_callchain_user()`, before any architecture-specific callchain function is invoked.
- **Added** a check `if (!current->mm) return;` immediately after storing the top-level entry, so that if `current->mm` is NULL (process already released memory), the function returns early without attempting to walk the user callchain.

## Relationships Between File Changes

The modifications are coordinated:
1. The top-level stack recording (IP from `regs`) is **moved** from the two architecture-specific functions (`callchain_32.c` and `callchain_64.c`) into the common `perf_callchain_user()` in `callchain.c`. This centralization ensures the entry is always stored, even when `current->mm` is NULL and the architecture-specific walk is skipped.
2. The addition of the `current->mm` NULL check prevents the kernel panic that occurred when the BPF profiling tool tried to access user pages while the process’s memory management structure was already freed. This fix mirrors a prior x86 commit.

Thus, the patch both fixes the NULL pointer dereference and preserves correct callchain recording by hoisting the initial entry storage to the common code.

Here is the root cause:
The bug occurs because `perf_callchain_user()` calls architecture-specific callchain walk functions (`perf_callchain_user_64` or `perf_callchain_user_32`) without first checking whether `current->mm` is NULL. During certain scenarios (e.g., process exit, memory release), `current->mm` can be null, causing the walk functions to attempt reading user memory through an invalid memory descriptor. This leads to a kernel NULL pointer dereference when accessing user pages (e.g., reading stack pointers). The specific panic occurred in `perf_callchain_user_64` while trying to read from user address space, triggered by a BPF profiling program.

Here is the patch:
 
 void
 perf_callchain_user(struct perf_callchain_entry_ctx *entry, struct pt_regs *regs)
 {
+	perf_callchain_store(entry, perf_arch_instruction_pointer(regs));
+
+	if (!current->mm)
+		return;
+
 	if (!is_32bit_task())
 		perf_callchain_user_64(entry, regs);
 	else
 		perf_callchain_user_32(entry, regs);
 }
